title: Post-quantum key exchange: proposed contract addendum
notice: Template, not legal advice: have your lawyer review it before you use it.
review: Written in plain English by SOQLAB and checked against NIST FIPS 203 and the IANA TLS Supported Groups registry for the facts it cites. It has not been reviewed by a lawyer for any country, and it does not say that any law or regulation calls for it.

placeholders.agreement: [name and date of the agreement this addendum belongs to]

intro: This addendum forms part of {agreement} between {buyer} and {vendor}. Where it conflicts with that agreement on the matters below, this addendum applies.

clauses.heading: Definitions
clauses.text: "Hybrid post-quantum key exchange" means a TLS key exchange that combines a classical elliptic-curve exchange with ML-KEM, the key-encapsulation mechanism standardised in NIST FIPS 203: X25519MLKEM768 (TLS supported group 0x11EC) or an equivalent hybrid group that uses a NIST-standardised ML-KEM parameter set. "Covered Endpoints" means: {endpoints}, and any hostname that replaces one of them for the same service.

clauses.heading: Commitment
clauses.text: By {date} (the "Target Date"), {vendor} will support hybrid post-quantum key exchange on every Covered Endpoint for TLS 1.3 connections, and will choose it whenever a client offers it.

clauses.heading: Re-verification
clauses.text: {buyer} may check any Covered Endpoint at any time with a public, read-only check, such as Morrow's public check at {check_url}. If such a check, made on or after the Target Date, shows a classical-only key exchange on a Covered Endpoint, {buyer} may send {vendor} the dated result, and {vendor} will reply within 30 days with either evidence that the result is wrong or a date by which it will be put right.

clauses.heading: Notice of cryptographic changes
clauses.text: {vendor} will give {buyer} at least 30 days' written notice before any planned change that removes or weakens hybrid post-quantum key exchange on a Covered Endpoint, and will tell {buyer} within 5 business days after an unplanned change that does so.

clauses.heading: Progress
clauses.text: Until the Target Date, {vendor} will tell {buyer} on request, at most once a quarter, how the work stands and whether the Target Date is still expected to be met.

sources.label: NIST FIPS 203, Module-Lattice-Based Key-Encapsulation Mechanism Standard (August 2024)
IANA, Transport Layer Security (TLS) Parameters: TLS Supported Groups (X25519MLKEM768 is 0x11EC)
